newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Most Bangladeshis safe from Malaysia crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Most Bangladeshis safe from Malaysia crackdown.

text.p: The majority of Bangladesh workers in Malaysia held valid work permits and were not at risk from a crackdown on illegal immigrants, a senior Bangladesh government official said on Thursday.

Malaysia started a nationwide blitz on February 1 to round up foreigners without valid work-permits after the lapse of a deadline for about one million illegal workers to leave the country or face prosecution.

"Bangladeshi workers have earned good reputation abroad, particularly in Malaysia. So there is less possibility we face problems with our workers in Malaysia," Mahe Alam, secretary of the Ministry of Labour and Manpower, told Reuters on return from a visit to Kuala Lumpur.
Alam held talks last week with Malaysia's Home and Labour secretaries during a visit to investigate the fate of Bangladeshis in Malaysia.
Officials say money sent home by about two million Bangladeshis working abroad, including in Malaysia, contribute significantly to the country's foreign exchange income.
Expatriate Bangladeshis remit home around $1 billion on average a year. The country's current foreign exchange reserves stand at nearly $2 billion.
Alam said Malaysia was likely to restart recruiting Bangladeshi workers soon after the current ban on manpower import was waived.

An executive with the official Bangladesh Overseas Employment Services Limited told Reuters that Malaysia recruited about 200,000 Bangladeshi workers through it and legally run private agencies. They all have been employed.
An unspecified number of Bangladeshis also entered Malaysia illegally, Alam said, but he could not give their number.
He dismissed recent newspaper reports that over 200,000 Bangladeshis were working or seeking jobs in Malaysia after travelling there with illegal documents.
